corridor: A carpeted hallway runs ahead, patterned in swirls designed by someone who hated eyes.
Velvet ropes on brass posts fold the corridor into a queue for nothing. You follow it anyway. Everyone does.
The hallway is lined with framed photos of smiling staff. The smiles have been retouched so often they've worn through.
A long service corridor, all scuffed walls and room-service trays left out since before the world ended.
The carpet in this passage is warm, slightly soft, and gives under your feet a little more than carpet should.
A corridor of identical doors, each with a DO NOT DISTURB sign. Behind one of them, something is very disturbed.
The hall slopes gently downward. The signs say it doesn't.
chamber: A vast check-in hall opens up, with a marble counter long enough to have its own weather.
You come out into an atrium so tall the chandeliers fade into haze before the ceiling does.
A ballroom spreads out under a mirrored ceiling. Your reflection up there is half a step behind you.
The lounge is all deep armchairs and low tables, arranged for a conversation nobody has had in years.
A fountain court, its basin full of coins and something that keeps moving them around.
A conference room with a hundred chairs facing a lectern. The slide on the screen is stuck on WELCOME!
A breakfast room with the buffet still out. The eggs have achieved a kind of permanence.
small: A cramped coat check, hangers clinking gently with no draft to move them.
A gift shop the size of a closet, stocked with snow globes of this exact lobby.
A concierge nook with a little brass bell. You know better than to ring it. You almost ring it.
An ice machine alcove. The machine drops one cube every few seconds, forever, like a heartbeat.
A phone booth with a velvet seat and a receiver hanging off the hook, breathing.
A powder room in pink marble, every mirror fogged from the other side.

sights: A welcome banner sags overhead: WELCOME, VALUED GUEST! Someone has crossed out GUEST and written MEAL.
Luggage carts stand abandoned in a ring, as if they were having a meeting and you interrupted.
The floor tiles have hairline cracks that all point the same way: down.
A brass floor drain is set into the marble, polished to a shine. Something under it is polished too.
Complimentary mints sit in crystal bowls. Every bowl is full. Nobody has ever taken one and stayed to describe it.
A potted palm has grown straight through its pot and into the floor, like it was looking for something.
Name badges are scattered across the carpet, all blank except for the word HELLO.
A digital sign cycles through the day's events: ORIENTATION. ORIENTATION. ORIENTATION. EVACUATION (CANCELLED).
The carpet has a stain shaped like a person lying down. It has been vacuumed around, very carefully.
A courtesy table offers coffee, tea and a third urn labelled DO NOT.
A podium sign reads PLEASE WAIT TO BE CONSUMED. CONSUMED is a sticker over SEATED, and the sticker is new.
A grand piano plays itself, badly, one key at a time, as if remembering a song it was only told about.
Lost-luggage tags drift across the floor in a breeze that comes from below.
A suggestion box overflows with folded notes. The top one says LET US OUT in perfect cursive.
The wallpaper is tiny repeated smiles. Up close, some of them have teeth.
A row of elevators all show the same floor number, which is a symbol that isn't a number.
Room keys hang in a glass case, each tagged with a name and a date. The dates are all today.
A fire extinguisher cabinet holds a neatly folded tablecloth and a note: IN CASE OF HUNGER.
The marble floor has been patched in one place with something pinker and softer than marble.
A brochure rack offers EXCITING EXCURSIONS: FLOOR 2, FLOOR 3, FLOOR 4, and a blank one that's been handled a lot.
sounds: Somewhere, a muzak version of a song you almost remember loops back on itself mid-chorus.
A soft ding from an elevator that never opens.
The floor gives a long, damp sigh, like a sleeper turning over.
A vacuum cleaner runs in a distant room, though there's no one to push it.
A desk bell rings once, politely, from somewhere you haven't been yet.
Ice clinks into a bucket in another room, steadily, forever.
The PA reads out a name, laughs, and says, "Oh, never mind."
Applause from an empty ballroom, going on a little too long.
The wheels of a luggage cart squeak past behind the wall.
A low hum comes up through your shoes. The walls are humming the same note.
Somebody is gargling in the drains. Somebody large.
A recorded voice welcomes you, then welcomes you, then welcomes you.
A revolving door turns somewhere, slowly, with nobody in it.
Laughter from a conference room, all on the same beat, like a laugh track.
smells: Lobby perfume: lilies, carpet glue and the fear sweat of a thousand check-ins.
Burnt coffee from an urn that has been on since the apocalypse.
The warm, yeasty smell of a breath that isn't yours.
Industrial air freshener losing a war with something underneath it.
Chlorine from a pool nobody has found.
Fresh-baked cookies. There are no cookies. There have never been cookies.
Damp carpet and old pennies.
Hand sanitizer, and under it, rot.
Bleach. Too much bleach, as if someone were making a point.
Room-service fries, cold and congealed and somehow still hopeful.
Brass polish, and a wet, meaty warmth from the drain grates.
Lavender, the kind they put in rooms where people get bad news.

stairwell: A staff-only stairwell behind a mirrored door, propped open with a rubber wedge and a note: GOING DOWN? ALWAYS.
The emergency stairs are lit by green EXIT signs that point down, insistently, from every angle.
A service stair spirals down past a sign reading GUESTS BEYOND THIS POINT ARE NO LONGER GUESTS.
The stairwell smells of cold concrete and new beginnings, which is worse than it sounds.
A grand staircase sweeps down into the dark, red carpet and all, like the lobby is seeing you out.
safe: A members-only lounge with a real lock, a working kettle and a sign: NO COMBAT IN THE LOUNGE, PLEASE. It's the please that sells it.
A staff break room: vending machine, a couch with a dent in it, a corkboard of shift schedules for a staff that isn't coming back.
A quiet guest room with the bed made and a chocolate on the pillow. The door locks from the inside. You check it four times.
The hush in here is the expensive kind. Even the floor stops breathing for a while.
treasure: A bellhop's trolley is still loaded with luggage, and nobody has come to claim any of it.
A display case of COMPLIMENTARY GIFTS sits unlocked. The word complimentary is doing a lot of work.
Behind the concierge desk, a safe hangs open like a mouth after the dentist.
puzzle: A wall of room keys on numbered hooks, a few of them swaying though nothing touched them.
A seating chart on an easel shows every table full but one, and that one has your name on it.
A thermostat panel with forty dials, all set to different temperatures, all labelled COMFORT.
npc: A cardboard cutout of a smiling greeter stands by the door. It's been turned to face you. You didn't see anyone turn it.
A guest book lies open on a stand, a pen on a chain beside it. The last entry is still wet.
empty: Nothing here but carpet, and the carpet seems fine with that.
An empty room with a single folding chair facing the wall, like it's being punished.
Just a draft, coming up through the floor vents, warm as breath.

trapTypes.name: Revolving Door
trapTypes.spotted: The revolving door is turning on its own, faster than a door should. You wait for it to tire and slip through between blades.
trapTypes.triggered: The revolving door grabs you mid-step, spins you three full turns and spits you out into the wall.
trapTypes.avoided: The door lunges. You don't. It spins on, sulking.

trapTypes.name: Hissing Radiator
trapTypes.spotted: The radiator under the window is rattling like it wants to say something. You give it room.
trapTypes.triggered: The radiator blows its valve and steams you like a dumpling.
trapTypes.avoided: Steam blasts the spot you were standing in a second ago.

trapTypes.name: Loose Chandelier
trapTypes.spotted: The chandelier overhead is hanging by one bolt and its own dignity. You walk around underneath it.
trapTypes.triggered: Crystal and brass come down on you like an expensive opinion.
trapTypes.avoided: The chandelier lands where you were, in a burst of very beautiful shrapnel.

trapTypes.name: Honest Wet Floor Sign
trapTypes.spotted: A yellow WET FLOOR sign, and for once it's telling the truth. You take the long way round.
trapTypes.triggered: Your feet go out from under you on marble polished with something that isn't polish.
trapTypes.avoided: You skate, wobble and somehow keep it.

trapTypes.name: Hungry Drain
trapTypes.spotted: One of the brass drains is open a crack too wide, and its edges are wet. You step over it.
trapTypes.triggered: The drain grate snaps shut on your ankle. There are teeth under the brass.
trapTypes.avoided: The grate snaps at the air beside your foot.

trapTypes.name: Frayed Service Cable
trapTypes.spotted: A cable runs under the carpet where the carpet is scorched. You don't step on the scorch.
trapTypes.triggered: The carpet bites you with electricity.
trapTypes.avoided: The carpet sparks behind your heel.

workbenchLines: A banquet table has been turned into a workbench: a vise clamped to one end, a tablecloth over the stains, a sign reading STAFF CRAFT NIGHT.
Behind the bell desk there's a luggage repair bench: clamps, rivets, a coffee can of screws and a strong smell of glue.
The maintenance office has a pegboard workbench. Every tool's outline is painted on the wall. Most of the tools are gone. The outlines stayed.

corridor: The aisle runs between shelves so tall and so full they lean together overhead like gossiping drunks.
A tunnel of stacked cardboard boxes, each labelled with a date and the word UNCLAIMED.
A conveyor belt runs down the middle of this passage, carrying single shoes past you one at a time, toward nowhere.
The corridor is lined with lockers, all of them humming faintly, none of them yours.
A narrow canyon of lost umbrellas, some open, some shut, rustling in a wind that isn't there.
chamber: A sorting hall opens up, with chutes in the ceiling dropping things onto a pile the size of a house: keys, phones, teeth.
A vast storage bay, shelving in every direction, and a ladder on rails that rolls slowly by itself.
The claims floor is a sea of numbered bins under a scoreboard that reads ITEMS RETURNED: 0.
An intake hall where a hundred cardboard boxes wait in rows, each with a name crossed out.
A baggage carousel turns in the middle of the hall, carrying one suitcase around and around. It's been waiting a long time.
small: A claims booth with a sliding window and a bell. A sign reads: DESCRIBE YOUR ITEM IN DETAIL. NO, MORE DETAIL.
A cubby room, every cubby stuffed with a single glove.
A key cabinet, hundreds of keys on hooks, all of them vibrating very slightly.
A little tag office: tag guns, string, a stamp that says FOUND and one that says GONE.

sights: A pile of phones, all lit, all showing the same missed call.
A shelf of jars holds lost teeth, sorted by owner. The labels are in a handwriting you almost recognize.
A box marked WEDDING RINGS is full to the brim and somehow still accepting more.
Claim tags drift in the corners like snow, every one filled in: FOUND BY: THE FLOOR.
A stack of name badges from earlier crawlers is held together with a rubber band. The top one just says D.
Someone has built a little shrine out of lost reading glasses, all of them facing the same drain.
A rack of coats, every pocket turned out, every lining slit.
A wall of photos pulled from lost wallets: families, pets, and one photo of a cracked handheld on a desk.
A floor drain wears a lost-and-found tag: FOUND, ALIVE, DO NOT FEED.
Hundreds of single socks are pinned to a corkboard in pairs that don't match.
A shopping cart full of lost hats rolls an inch, stops, and rolls another inch.
An inventory ledger lies open. Every entry for the last hundred pages reads: 1 x CRAWLER, UNCLAIMED.
A pram full of umbrellas, folded like sleeping bats, every handle tagged.
The lowest shelves are damp and swollen, as if the floor has been drinking from them.
sounds: Paper rustles on every shelf at once, like a crowd turning to look.
A phone buzzes somewhere in a box of phones. Then all of them do.
A tag gun clicks in another aisle: click, click, click, filing something.
Something heavy is dragged across the floor above, slowly, like furniture with regrets.
A drain gurgles a word. It might be your name. It might be "more".
A distant voice reads out an item description: "One crawler, slightly used."
The shelves creak as if they're breathing in.
Keys jingle in a cabinet with nobody near it.
A conveyor belt starts, runs for three seconds, and stops.
The hum under the floor is lower here, and closer.
smells: Mothballs, old leather and the insides of other people's pockets.
Damp cardboard. Miles of it.
Lost perfume: a hundred bottles' worth, all slightly turned.
Rubber from a mountain of lost galoshes.
Dust so old it has its own smell, like a library that gave up.
Wet wool, and a faint warm breath from the drains.
Pennies, gum and lint.
Someone's lost lunch, unclaimed since the apocalypse and very much still with us.
Ink from the FOUND stamp, sharp and fresh, as if it was used a second ago.
Salt, faintly, from somewhere far below.

stairwell: A stairwell door with a claim tag hung on the handle: FOUND, ONE WAY DOWN, NO RETURNS.
The stairs down are stacked with boxes on every step, leaving a path exactly one crawler wide.
A spiral stair winds down through a hole cut in the shelving, labelled MISC.
safe: A locked claims office with a cot, a kettle and a sign: LOST ITEMS ONLY BEYOND THIS POINT. YOU COUNT.
A storeroom someone turned into a bedroom with a mattress, a lamp and a row of unclaimed teddy bears for company.
The quiet in here is total. Even the paper stops rustling, as if it's been told you're off the clock.
treasure: A shelf marked VALUABLES (UNCLAIMED) is still mostly full, which is either luck or bait.
A lockbox stands open, its contents sorted into neat little piles by somebody who left in a hurry.
puzzle: A wall of numbered cubbies, and a claim ticket on the floor with a number that isn't on the wall.
A sorting machine with three chutes labelled MINE, YOURS and NOBODY'S. It's waiting for you to choose.
npc: A claims window with a bell, and behind the frosted glass a shape that has been waiting for you specifically.
A note pinned to a shelf: I'M IN THE NEXT AISLE. DON'T LOOK FOR ME. -D.
empty: An empty shelf, the only empty shelf, and the dust on it is shaped like something that was just taken.
Nothing here but a coat rack with one coat on it, still warm.

trapTypes.name: Box Avalanche
trapTypes.spotted: The boxes at the top of this stack are leaning in at you, very interested. You go round.
trapTypes.triggered: The stack comes down: forty years of unclaimed boxes, all at once, all on you.
trapTypes.avoided: The boxes bury the spot where you were standing. Something in one of them says "ow".

trapTypes.name: Tag Gun Nest
trapTypes.spotted: Three tag guns are wired to a tripwire across the aisle. You step over it and feel deeply unlabelled.
trapTypes.triggered: Tag guns fire from the shelves and tag you, thoroughly, in places tags don't go.
trapTypes.avoided: A burst of claim tags thwacks into the shelving where your head was.

trapTypes.name: Drain Mouth
trapTypes.spotted: The drain in the middle of the aisle has gums. You decide you don't need that part of the aisle.
trapTypes.triggered: The drain opens wider than any drain should and closes on your leg.
trapTypes.avoided: The drain snaps shut on nothing and makes a sulky wet sound.

trapTypes.name: Tangle of Lost Chargers
trapTypes.spotted: A knot of lost phone chargers is plugged into each other in a loop and sparking. You leave it to its business.
trapTypes.triggered: A hundred lost chargers find their way into you all at once.
trapTypes.avoided: The chargers spark at your heels and go back to charging nothing.

workbenchLines: A sorting bench with clamps, string, a tag gun bolted down and a sign: REPAIRS TO UNCLAIMED ITEMS ONLY. Everything here qualifies.
A cobbler's bench for lost shoes, still strewn with tacks and glue, a single heel in the vise.

corridor: A drive aisle runs off into the dark, ankle-deep in water with a rainbow sheen on top.
The ramp curls downward, and the water gets deeper with every level the painted numbers claim you've passed.
A low tunnel between parking decks, pipes dripping onto the roofs of cars that will never leave.
The pedestrian walkway is painted with yellow footprints that walk confidently into the wall.
A fire lane, clear for once, which is exactly what makes it suspicious.
chamber: A parking level spreads out under a low ceiling, cars parked nose to tail, every one of them with its hazards blinking.
A drowned car wash: brushes hanging still, the water around them brown and moving on its own.
The valet lot is a lake. A podium stands in the middle of it, dry, with a bell on top.
A pay station plaza, three machines in a row, all of them saying INSERT TICKET to nobody.
A tow yard, cars stacked three high, every one with a ticket on the windshield fluttering in no wind.
small: A ticket booth with a sliding window, a stool, and a single stamped ticket pinned to the corkboard like a trophy.
An attendant's hut: a space heater, a crossword, a cold cup of coffee with a skin on it.
A stairwell landing that smells of wet concrete, with a puddle that doesn't reflect you.
An electrical room humming with breakers. One of them is labelled DO NOT. It's on.

sights: A sedan with every window fogged from the inside, and a handprint slowly appearing on the glass.
Parking lines are painted on the ceiling, as if the garage was built upside down and nobody noticed.
A pay station screen reads INSERT TICKET. INSERT TICKET. INSERT YOURSELF.
Hubcaps float in a slow circle around a drain, like fish around a feeder.
A row of cars all have their headlights on, every one pointed at the same pillar.
Soggy parking tickets paper the walls like scales.
A rope barrier blocks off a reserved bay with nothing in it but a puddle shaped like a car.
The water is higher on one side of the level than the other, and it isn't level about it.
A valet key box hangs open, every hook empty but one, and that key is warm.
A sign says COMPACT CARS ONLY. Under it, someone has compacted a car.
Oil drips from the ceiling in slow black beads that land, every time, on the same spot.
A parking meter has been fed so many coins it has started to bulge.
sounds: Water drips from the levels above, echoing like a slow clock.
A car alarm starts somewhere, cycles through every sound it knows, and stops mid-whoop.
Tires squeal on a ramp you can't see, though there's no car.
Three honks, from deep below. Then three more, closer.
Water sloshes up the ramp in a long, slow wave, then drains back down.
A ticket machine prints a ticket, then another, then another, faster and faster.
An engine turns over somewhere and doesn't catch. It keeps trying.
The concrete groans, a long low note, like something heavy shifting in its sleep.
A puddle burps.
The PA plays the garage's hold music, which is just the sound of rain.
smells: Gasoline, brine and wet concrete.
Hot tire rubber, though nothing here has moved in years.
Exhaust, old and trapped, like a breath held too long.
Mildew in the upholstery of a thousand drowned cars.
Salt so strong you can taste it.
Antifreeze, sweet and wrong.
Car air freshener, pine, fighting something that won't lose.
Rust, and under it, something warm and fleshy coming up through the drains.

stairwell: A stairwell door marked LEVEL B-SOMETHING, propped open with a traffic cone.
The stairs down are dry, which down here is a luxury, and there's a sign: EXIT. NOT THAT ONE. THIS ONE.
A cargo elevator with the doors pried open and a ladder bolted down the shaft.
safe: An attendant's office with a lock, a dry floor, a cot and a space heater that still works. You could cry.
A locked storage cage full of traffic cones and a single camp bed. The cones form a perimeter. Someone was serious.
The quiet in here is thick and dry. Out there, the water keeps talking. In here, it doesn't.
treasure: A car with its trunk open and its contents still inside, which in a garage like this counts as a miracle.
A lost-ticket office safe, its door hanging open and a trail of coins leading out of it.
puzzle: A pay station with three slots, three buttons and three instructions that contradict each other.
A wall map of the garage with YOU ARE HERE in two places, and both of them are wrong.
npc: A parking attendant's booth with the window open a crack, and a voice inside humming the hold music.
A valet podium with a little sign: BACK IN 5 MINUTES. The sign is very old.
empty: An empty bay with a perfect dry rectangle where a car used to be.
Nothing here but water, standing very still, waiting to see what you do.

trapTypes.name: Flooded Pothole
trapTypes.spotted: The water here is darker in a perfect circle. You don't step in the circle.
trapTypes.triggered: The floor isn't there. You drop to your waist in cold, oily water.
trapTypes.avoided: Your foot finds the edge of a hole and you pull it back, heart going.

trapTypes.name: Car Alarm Ambush
trapTypes.spotted: Every car on this row has its alarm light blinking in time. You tiptoe.
trapTypes.triggered: Every alarm on the row goes off at once, and for a moment the noise is the only thing in the world.
trapTypes.avoided: The alarms go off as you clear the row, and you're already round the corner with your ears ringing.

trapTypes.name: Oil Spill
trapTypes.spotted: A slick of motor oil covers the floor here, shining like a promise. You go round.
trapTypes.triggered: You hit the oil and the floor stops being a floor.
trapTypes.avoided: You slide, catch a wing mirror, and stay up.

trapTypes.name: Low Clearance Beam
trapTypes.spotted: A sign reads LOW CLEARANCE. The beam under it has hair on it. You duck.
trapTypes.triggered: You find the low clearance with your face.
trapTypes.avoided: You duck just in time and feel the beam ruffle your hair.

trapTypes.name: Submerged Cable
trapTypes.spotted: The water here fizzes faintly. A cable runs down into it. You find another way.
trapTypes.triggered: The water is live, and so, briefly, are you.
trapTypes.avoided: The water crackles behind you as you haul yourself onto a car bonnet.

workbenchLines: A mechanic's bench in a service bay: a vise, a socket set missing every useful size, and a lift with a car still on it.
A tyre shop workbench, patches and glue and a compressor that still coughs into life.
